h1: The 6 Best Fatboy Holsters for Larger-Waist Carry in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 holsters for larger-waist concealed carry, scored on ride height, retention, material, gun fit and comfort, from under $30 up.
summary: The JX Tactical Fat Guy for the Glock 19 is the holster to buy if you carry on a larger waist, with a low-ride design, adjustable retention and a model-specific fit. The JX for the Sig P365X Macro is the pick for a slimmer pistol, the Relentless Tactical Defender is the best leather holster that fits many guns, and the IBYADO chest holster is the fallback when a waistband will not work.
intro: The usual advice for larger-bodied carriers is to buy the same holster everyone else wears and a bigger belt. That is the mistake. A bigger midsection changes where the grip lands, how far the pistol prints, and whether appendix carry is even workable. Holsters that sit high on the belt tip the grip forward over a stomach, so the ride height and the contour of the body-facing side matter more than the badge on the box.

This ranking looks at six holsters with that problem in mind. We reviewed the spec sheets and listings for ride height, retention adjustment, material, belt clip, gun compatibility and price bracket, and we call out where a listing gives no detail. Every holster here must fully cover the trigger guard, and you should confirm that for your exact pistol before you carry.

products.name: JX Tactical Fat Guy Holster for Glock 19, BK, RH | Inside the Waistband Holster, Proudly Made in the USA, Sits Lower in the Waistline for a Comfortable Concealed Carry
products.verdict: The only holster here designed around a low waistline, made for the most common compact pistol.
products.description:
This is an inside-the-waistband holster, right-hand, made in the USA for a specific pistol, the Glock 19. Its calling card is a low-ride position that seats the gun deeper against the body, plus a Monoblock clip, an ergonomic contour for appendix carry, adjustable retention and room for common red dot configurations.

It ranks first because of the design intent. Most IWB holsters are cut for a flat waist, and on a larger one they push the grip outward where a shirt cannot hide it. Lower ride and a contoured body side counter that. Against the Relentless Defender it gives up universal fit: this is a model-specific holster, so it only works if you own that exact pistol. In return you get adjustable draw tension, which a one-size leather pouch cannot offer.

Buy it if you carry a Glock 19 and need all-day comfort over a larger stomach. The caveats are the $50 to $100 price and right-hand only configuration, and the listing does not state the shell material, so check that before you buy.
products.idealFor: Glock 19 owners who carry daily and want the grip tucked low.
products.skipIf: You switch between several pistols or carry left-handed.

products.name: JX Tactical Fat Guy Holster for Sig Sauer P365X Macro, BK, RH | Inside the Waistband Holster, Proudly Made in the USA, Sits Lower in the Waistline for a Comfortable Concealed Carry
products.verdict: The same low-ride design, shaped for a thinner pistol that disappears more easily.
products.description:
This version of the JX Tactical design is built for the Sig Sauer P365X Macro, with the same low-ride seating, Monoblock clip, appendix-oriented contour and adjustable retention as the Glock 19 model. It is inside the waistband, right-hand, and made in the USA.

It takes second place only because the pistol is a smaller platform than the Glock 19. A Macro generally prints less on a big torso, so the holster and gun combine into a slimmer package than the Glock holster can manage, and that is the whole case for choosing it. We rank it just below the Glock model because the Glock 19 has far more owners, so the broader set of spare mags, lights and aftermarket parts sits behind that pistol. If you already carry the P365X Macro, though, nothing here fits it better.

Pick it if you want maximum concealment from a thinner pistol. As with the others in this family, the listing gives no shell material, so confirm it, and the red dot support is described only as popular configurations.

products.name: Relentless Tactical The Defender Leather IWB Holster | Made in USA | Fits Glock 17 19 19X 22 26 43 43X 45 | Taurus GC3 | S&W M&P Shield | Canik TP9 Elite | Plus All Similar Sized Handguns | Oak RH
products.verdict: A broad-fit leather IWB made in the USA, for under $50.
products.description:
The Defender is a leather IWB pouch in an oak finish, right-hand, made in the USA. The listing names a huge fit list: Glock 17, 19, 19X, 22, 26, 43, 43X and 45, plus the Taurus GC3, S&W M&P Shield, Springfield XD and XDS, H&K VP9 and Sig P226 and P229 and other similar-sized handguns in 9mm, .40 and .45.

It ranks third because it covers the most guns for the least money, in the $30 to $50 bracket, but a one-size leather pouch does not have the adjustable retention of the JX holsters, and it rides at the height you give it. Leather also softens with wear, which gives a more molded feel over time, and it is gentler on the body than a hard shell. Its tradeoff against the Rabray is a fuller maker pedigree and a wider listed fit.

It suits a carrier who owns more than one pistol and wants a single comfortable holster. The caveat is a mouth that can collapse after you draw if the leather has no reinforcement, so confirm that you can reholster one-handed, and check your exact model against the maker's list.

products.name: JX Tactical Fat Guy Holster for CANIK Mete MC9, CB, RH | Inside the Waistband Holster, Proudly Made in the USA, Sits Lower in the Waistline for a Comfortable Concealed Carry
products.verdict: The low-ride JX design for a gun that few holster makers cut for.
products.description:
This one is for the Canik Mete MC9, using the same JX Tactical low-ride seating, Monoblock clip, appendix contour, adjustable retention and red dot allowance as the other two JX holsters. It is right-hand and inside the waistband, and it is made in the USA.

The score sits below the other JX models for one reason: pistol choice, not holster quality. Canik owners have far fewer holster options than Glock owners, and a model-specific holster is the best way to get a lower ride and a tight fit. The design itself is as good as the Glock 19 version. What you lose compared with the Relentless Defender is flexibility: sell the pistol and this holster is dead weight.

Buy it if you own the Mete MC9 and want a larger-waist-friendly holster that is not a generic pouch. The caveats are the right-hand only listing and no stated shell material. The listing also gives no detail on the finish designated CB.
products.idealFor: Canik Mete MC9 owners who want a tailored larger-waist holster.
products.skipIf: You may swap pistols or want a leather feel.

products.name: IWB Leather Holster, Genuine Leather Gun Holster for Glock 19/42/43X Ruger LC9S/Security 9/Max 9, Sig P365/P320/P220, Taurus G2C/G3C/GX4 Springfield XD/XDS/Hellcat and Similar Sized Handguns
products.verdict: Genuine leather IWB with a reinforced mouth and sweat guard, under $30.
products.description:
The Rabray is a genuine leather IWB holster with a reinforced top that stays open for reholstering and a sweat guard shield between the gun and your body. It fits many compact handguns in 9mm, .40, .45 and .380 with barrels of 3.1 to 4.25 inches, including the Glock 19 and 43X, Sig P365 and P320 and Springfield Hellcat.

It places fifth because it is the cheapest leather option and the sweat guard matters on a larger body, where perspiration against the gun and holster is a real maintenance issue. The reinforced mouth is the feature that rescues it from the usual one-handed reholster problem. The limits are strict: the listing says it will not fit guns carrying a laser, light or tall front sight, which rules out many modern setups, and unlike the JX models it has no adjustable retention.

It is the right buy for a first holster on a tight budget under $30. Do not buy it if your pistol wears a weapon light.
cons: No laser, light or tall sights
products.idealFor: Budget buyers carrying a plain compact pistol.
products.skipIf: Your pistol has a weapon light or laser.

products.name: Universal Chest Holster for Pistols, Shoulder Holster for Hiking, Camping, Hunting
products.verdict: A neoprene chest rig for people whose waistband is simply not an option.
products.description:
The IBYADO is a right-handed chest holster in neoprene and cotton webbing with an adjustable shoulder strap and a chest mount. It is meant for hiking, camping and hunting, and it moves the pistol off the belt entirely, which sidesteps the stomach problem altogether.

It ranks last because it is a different tool. A chest rig is outdoor gear, not concealed carry, and it is a universal fit with little listed about retention, so you cannot assume a secure hold for your exact pistol. What it does well is solve a problem the waistband holsters cannot: if a belly blocks appendix carry and a belt rides under a pack hip strap, the chest is the one place the gun sits clear. Against the JX holsters it is cheaper at under $30 but far less refined.

Buy it for trail use over a jacket. The caveat: universal fit means you should confirm trigger coverage and security with an unloaded gun before it goes near a hike.
pros: Works under a pack hip belt
products.idealFor: Hikers and hunters who cannot wear a belt holster.
products.skipIf: You need a holster for daily concealment.

whatMatters.detail: Ride height is how far the gun sits above or below the belt line. On a larger waist, a high ride tilts the grip outward and prints through a shirt, while a lower ride tucks the grip closer to the body. The JX Tactical models advertise a low ride; on other listings, look for the words low ride or deep concealment, since a plain IWB pouch gives no number.

Retention is the force that holds the pistol until you draw. Too loose and the gun can move when you bend or walk; too tight and a draw under stress is clumsy. Adjustable retention, listed on the JX Tactical holsters, lets you set it once. Fixed leather pouches like the Defender and the Rabray rely on how the leather breaks in.

A holster must fully cover the trigger guard so nothing can enter it while the gun is stored. This is the first safety test for any carry rig, and a universal holster cannot promise it for every pistol. Prefer model-specific fits, and with a universal one like the IBYADO, check coverage with an unloaded gun before use.

Leather softens and absorbs sweat, but it needs a reinforced mouth so it does not collapse when empty. Hard shells hold their shape but can be firmer against skin. Neoprene is flexible and water-tolerant. Read the material on the listing; the JX holsters leave it unstated, which is worth asking the seller about.

Red dots, lasers and lights change the holster shape you need. The JX holsters mention optic compatibility, while the Rabray states it does not fit guns with a laser, light or high front sight. If your pistol carries an accessory, match it to the holster description exactly, because a near fit is not a fit.

faq.a: Not as listed. The three JX Tactical models, the Relentless Defender and the IBYADO chest holster are all right-hand versions. Check for a left-hand option on the listing before ordering, and do not flip a right-hand holster.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with larger-waist carry?
faq.a: Forcing appendix carry with a holster built for a flat waist. The grip then pushes outward and prints. Choose a low-ride contoured holster like the JX Tactical Glock 19 model, or move the holster toward the hip.

faq.q: Is the JX Tactical worth it over the Relentless Defender?
faq.a: If you carry a single pistol every day, yes. The JX has adjustable retention and a low ride built in. The Relentless Defender costs less and covers many guns, but it relies on leather break-in for hold.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Mount the clip over the belt, then seat the holster at the position that lets the grip clear your waist. On the JX models, adjust retention until the gun holds when you lean and still draws cleanly. Always do this unloaded.

faq.q: How should I care for a leather holster?
faq.a: Wipe off sweat and let leather like the Rabray dry fully before you reinsert the gun. Avoid heat sources, and check the reinforced mouth for cracks. A neoprene rig like the IBYADO can be rinsed and air dried.

faq.q: Can I use a pistol with a light or laser?
faq.a: Only if the holster says so. The Rabray explicitly excludes guns with lasers, lights or high front sights, and no listing here promises light-bearing fit apart from optic notes on the JX holsters. Match your exact setup.

finalTake: If you carry a Glock 19 or a P365X Macro on a larger waist, buy the matching JX Tactical holster and set the retention to your hand. The Relentless Tactical Defender is the pick for owners of several pistols who like leather, and the Rabray covers a first holster for less than $30. The IBYADO chest rig is for trails, not daily concealment. Confirm trigger guard coverage for your exact gun before you carry any of them.
